sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
In Ingolstadt the garage company IFG sets garage fees. Its administrative board decided on 8 June 2026 to raise fees at inner-city garages from 1 September 2026, citing renovation, modernisation and higher maintenance, energy and property-tax costs. The first 30 minutes stay free and the station car parks stay at €2.50 a day [14]. A May 2026 blog report on the plan put the first hour in downtown garages at €2.50, up from €2.20, but we could not confirm those figures from IFG. The previous rise was in September 2023, the first since 2018, when 30-minute billing was introduced in five city-centre garages [3]. In 2021 IFG had cut fees in four garages to €1.00 an hour from June to October to help downtown businesses recover from the pandemic [0].

On transport, the city says a tram is presumably not viable within 15 years and a bus rapid transit system would carry considerable economic risk, so it is optimising the existing bus system [4]. A new Mobilitätsplan 2040+, started in early 2025, is due by the end of 2027 under EU rules for urban nodes [12]. Michael Kern (CSU) won the mayoral election on 23 February 2025 with 64.2% against Christian De Lapuente (SPD), and was due to take over from Christian Scharpf on 1 March [6]. The Ludwigstraße pedestrian-zone project finished its third phase at the end of 2025, with the fourth and fifth postponed [21].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
IFG has been modernising its facilities. The new Parkhaus Arena was partly opened on 20 January 2025, fully cashless and ticketless with plate recognition, with about 330 spaces at that stage [7]. IFG announced a modernised guidance system with 41 new signs in March 2025, to be completed in April [8]. From September 2025 it began rolling out ticketless plate recognition across its facilities, starting with the Hauptbahnhof Ost and West car parks [11]. From 1 February 2026 the free park-and-ride bus ended for Nordbahnhof and Festplatz because of low use, and continues at Reduit Tilly [13]. IFG has 56 charging points in its car parks, and as private car parks they are excluded from Bavaria's free-parking rule for electric vehicles [10].

The centre faces demand pressures. Around 61,500 people commute in each day, down from over 65,000 in 2018, with 70% from the three neighbouring districts, and out-commuting has risen from about 20,000 to over 25,000 [22]. IFG bought the empty former Kaufhof building on Ludwigstraße in 2024, which the then mayor called a considerable setback for the city centre [5]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
IFG Ingolstadt, the city's parkIN operator, runs 14 parking facilities with over 7,000 spaces, and all nine car parks in our data belong to it [17]. Five are within 500 m of the Rathausplatz (2,110 spaces) and one more within 1 km. The Tiefgarage Congress has 719 spaces, a monthly pass of €99 and short-term rates of €2.50 to €14.50 [18]. Nordbahnhof lists 252 spaces at €2.50 per 24 hours with the first 30 minutes free [19], against 230 in our feed.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 44% on weekdays and 36% at weekends. The fullest is Nordbahnhof (71%, probably commuters), followed by Hauptbahnhof West (59% on weekdays, 64% at weekends), Theater-West (48%), Reduit Tilly and Münster (both 43%). The emptiest are Schloss (30%), Theater-Ost (35%) and Hallenbad (36%). Within 500 m of the centre the average is 37%, against 71% at the Nordbahnhof 1 to 2 km out. Over the years Nordbahnhof rose from 22% in 2022 to 61% in 2025, and Hauptbahnhof West from 47% to 49%, while Hallenbad fell from 55% to 40% and Theater-Ost from 82% in 2022 to 33% in 2025. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ.
